questions.q: What is the difference between the goods trade deficit and the overall trade deficit?
questions.brief: The overall deficit adds trade in services (travel, transport, finance and the like), where the U.S. runs a surplus; give the latest month's goods deficit, services surplus and combined figure.

sources.label: Bureau of Economic Analysis, U.S. International Trade in Goods and Services, August 2026

questions.searched: who pays tariffs importer or exporter
questions.brief: Who owes the duty to the U.S. government (the importer, not the foreign seller) and when it is paid. Only who pays the government; not who ends up bearing the cost.

sources.label: U.S. Customs and Border Protection, Internet purchases
U.S. Customs and Border Protection, Entry summary and post-release processes

questions.q: Who decides tariffs, the President or Congress?
questions.searched: who decides tariffs president or congress
questions.brief: The Constitution gives Congress the power over duties; Congress has delegated some of it to the President by law, with conditions. Name the laws the sources name; no politicians.

sources.label: U.S. Constitution, Article I, Section 8 (National Archives)
Congressional Research Service, Congressional and Presidential Authority to Impose Import Tariffs

questions.q: What is the difference between Section 232 and Section 301 tariffs?
questions.brief: Which agency investigates, what each one must find (a threat to national security; an unfair foreign trade practice), and who then acts.

sources.label: Bureau of Industry and Security, Section 232 investigations
U.S. International Trade Commission, Section 232 and 301 trade actions in 2018

questions.q: What is the difference between a tariff and a duty?
questions.brief: Whether the two words mean the same thing in U.S. trade law, and what a tariff schedule is.

sources.label: Congressional Research Service, Congressional and Presidential Authority to Impose Import Tariffs
